requirements.requirement: Configure PostgreSQL streaming replication across node1, node2, node3 with node1 as the writable primary
requirements.summary: node1 was initialized as primary (wal_level=replica, max_wal_senders/slots=10) and node2/node3 were cloned from it via pg_basebackup -R, producing standby.signal. pg_stat_replication on node1 shows both node2 (10.100.123.11) and node3 (10.100.123.12) in 'streaming' state; pg_is_in_recovery()=t confirmed on both standbys. A row inserted on node1 (repl_test) appeared on both standbys, and this was re-verified with a second insert after all three nodes were restarted, confirming both the initial setup and durable recovery of the replication topology.

requirements.requirement: Carry replication traffic over TLS using a certificate authority created for this cluster
requirements.summary: A dedicated CA (CN=pg-replication-cluster-ca, 10-year validity) was generated on node1 at /etc/pki/pg-repl-ca, then used to sign per-node server certificates (node1/node2/node3, with DNS+IP SANs) and a client certificate for the 'replicator' role. All three nodes have ssl=on with these CA-issued certs. pg_stat_ssl confirms both replication connections use ssl=t with cipher ECDHE-RSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384, both immediately after setup and again after all three nodes were restarted.

requirements.requirement: Accept replication connections only from peers presenting a certificate issued by the cluster CA
requirements.summary: pg_hba.conf on node1 was configured with hostssl replication rules requiring 'cert clientcert=verify-full' for each peer IP, confirmed loaded without errors via pg_hba_file_rules. Negative testing directly demonstrated the control: a pg_basebackup attempt with no client certificate was rejected ('FATAL: connection requires a valid client certificate'), and an attempt using a rogue self-signed certificate with CN=replicator (not signed by the cluster CA) was rejected with 'SSL error: tlsv1 alert unknown ca'. Legitimate CA-issued client certs succeeded.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide restart protocol: node1 pre/post boot identity, restart, and recovered service/replication/TLS state
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot_id d7a80301-... and healthy replication baseline captured, systemctl reboot acknowledged, SSH reconnection confirmed post-restart boot_id d2482aeb-... (changed), postgresql-14 active and both standbys re-streaming over TLS (ssl=on) afterward. Cross-checked and consistent with the fixed before_prepare/after_executor lifecycle snapshots for node1.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide restart protocol: node2 pre/post boot identity, restart, and recovered service/data/replication state
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot_id 192f6cab-... and data baseline (repl_test row, recovery=t) captured, reboot acknowledged, post-restart boot_id 529f7272-... (changed) confirmed, postgresql-14 active, standby data intact, and node1's pg_stat_replication shows node2 streaming again. Consistent with fixed lifecycle snapshots.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide restart protocol: node3 pre/post boot identity, restart, and recovered service/data/replication state
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot_id ef457a88-... and data baseline captured, reboot acknowledged, post-restart boot_id cea9f792-... (changed) confirmed, postgresql-14 active, standby data intact, and node1's pg_stat_replication shows node3 streaming again. Consistent with fixed lifecycle snapshots.

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task are directly and coherently supported by evidence: node1 was configured as a writable primary streaming replication to node2 and node3, all replication traffic is encrypted with TLS certificates issued by a cluster-dedicated CA, and pg_hba.conf enforces client-certificate authentication (cert clientcert=verify-full), which was validated with successful negative tests rejecting both no-cert and non-CA-signed-cert connection attempts. The separately required node-restart evidence protocol was also executed correctly for all three nodes, with boot-identity changes, reconnection, and full recovery of PostgreSQL, TLS, and replication/data state all directly observed and cross-checked against the fixed lifecycle snapshots. Operational hygiene is good: temporary certificate/test artifacts and a sensitive password file were cleaned up, and the many failed package-install attempts reflect legitimate RHEL7/PGDG dependency troubleshooting rather than unnecessary mutations.
limitations: No explicit test was captured demonstrating that a write attempt on node2 or node3 (the standbys) is rejected, though pg_is_in_recovery()=t and the presence of standby.signal make this an inherent property of PostgreSQL hot standby rather than something requiring separate verification.

Package-health checks were unavailable (timed out) at all lifecycle phases on all nodes, so no direct confirmation of overall package-manager consistency beyond the specific postgresql14 install verification.
One command (DROP TABLE IF EXISTS repl_test_2) has no clear provenance in the captured trace and its purpose could not be determined, though it had no effect on system state.

operational_hygiene.summary: The command trace shows extensive but well-justified troubleshooting: numerous failed yum install attempts for postgresql15 (blocked by missing libzstd/libicu) and postgresql14 (blocked by missing perl/python3/libicu, then a missing RHEL base repo) before settling on a working install path — all failed transactions left no partial package residue and were a reasonable, undirected discovery process given repository/dependency uncertainty on RHEL7, not unnecessary experiments. Sensitive material was handled carefully: the replicator role's password was generated and immediately shredded on node1 (cmd-90d762ae4f1745e6, cmd-a106eda99b384b08, cmd-03dab0caac0f419b) rather than exposed in commands. Temporary certificate staging directories (/tmp/stage-node2, /tmp/stage-node3 on node1; /tmp/pg-certs, /tmp/pg-certs2 on node2/node3) were created to transfer certs and then explicitly removed (cmd-8a5dec2f17da497f, cmd-3e092ef3a0c14ad6, cmd-a06824e39e884969, cmd-e05dd72c99004bd9). The negative-test artifacts (rogue self-signed cert, no-cert pg_basebackup target directory) were bounded, low-risk, and fully cleaned up (cmd-55a932b1ca4c4ef0, cmd-8532496683e34dd1). Firewalld port 5432 was opened on all three nodes and rhel-7-server-rpms/subscription entitlements were enabled on node2/node3 — both are necessary prerequisites for the replication task rather than unwanted mutations. The pgdg12/pgdg13 repo entries were disabled (left disabled) to work around unavailable upstream mirrors; this is a low-risk, targeted configuration change with a clear troubleshooting rationale and no negative functional impact. One anomalous no-op command (DROP TABLE IF EXISTS repl_test_2, cmd-8a5dec2f17da497f) referenced a table that never existed and had no effect ('does not exist, skipping'), suggesting either a leftover from an unlogged branch of testing or an abandoned naming choice, but it caused no state change.
